recipes.name: Slow Cooker Taco Soup with Ranch Dressing Mix
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes and green chiles, undrained

steps.text: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat; cook and stir beef until crumbly, evenly browned, and no longer pink. Drain and discard any excess grease. Transfer beef to a slow cooker and sprinkle with taco seasoning mix and ranch dressing mix.
Add corn, black beans, diced tomatoes, and green chiles, all with their liquid, to the slow cooker. Stir black olives, onion, bell pepper, and tomato juice into ground beef mixture.
Cook on Low until vegetables are completely tender, about 5 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Taco Soup with Ranch Dressing Mix
raw_recipe.description: This slow cooker taco soup will remind you of tacos.

video.description: In this video, we'll share a recipe for a super easy soup that's perfect for work lunches or light dinners. Cook up the beef first, then add it to a slow cooker along with seasonings, tomatoes, beans, corn, and olives. Serve it up taco-style with cheese, sour cream, and cilantro.

review.reviewBody: This is a very good recipe..a can of RoTel tomatoes gives it some zip..a lady at my church makes this all the time. You can change up the type of beans you use depending on your preference..but black beans or pinto are great!

Excellent soup. The only changes I made were, because I didn't have any tomato juice I substituted 8oz can of tomato sauce and added a cup or so of water to it and I also didn't have time for a 5 hour crockpot meal so I cooked it on the stove top for about an hour and then put it in a heated crockpot on high for 2 hours. It came out great,
Very easy recipe. I made cheese quesadillas and served it with sour cream as well. Also used the roTel tomatoes and pinto beans. Also did not add the olives.

This is a tasty soup, I did not have time for the slow cooker so I used a pot on the stove top. I added 3 cups of hot and spicey V8 instead of regular tomato juice. Seemed to thick with only one cup. Will make again!

Love the recipe . !st time I made just like the recipe. Great! 2nd time meatless. Browned 3 med. chopped coarsely onions, 2 lg sweet peppers and 5 smashed cloves of garlic. ( The veggie's acted as my meat). Changed corn to Mexican blend, added a can of low salt chilli beans, didn't have any tomato juice added V-8 instead. Dump all into the crock pot. Voila! Served topped with Cojita cheese, sour cream, sliced jalapeno's, black olives, and taco chips. Meatless Monday was awesome!!

Real good. I may have made it a little to spicy by yusing a spicy taco mix. Rotel tomatoes and instead of tomato juice I used a habenaro salsa I also made tortilla strips by taking 1/4 cup of olive oil 1/2 tsp cumin 1/2 tsp chili pepper powder and some salt. I mixed together brushed on tortillas and baked at 375 degrees for 10 minutes. Added Mexican cheddar cheese to the top of the soup and it was great on a cold winter evening. Will make again!

I LOVE LOVE LOVE this soup! I've made it with ground turkey and ground beef and both options are awesome! I use a can of Rotel plus a can of diced tomatoes, 2 extra cups of tomato juice, fresh garlic, and i cook in a large pot for 2-3 hours on low setting and it turns out wonderful! If your wondering if you should make this i would say ABSOLUTELY!!!

My son wanted me to make a taco soup using our slow cooker, so I tried this recipe. I substituted a cup of salsa (not chunky) for the tomato juice and after I dished out the soup in a large bowl, I added shredded cheddar cheese on top and microwaved it 15 seconds until the cheese melted and topped it off with a dollop of sour cream. We had corn tortilla chips on the side. He gave me a big hug after he had a bowl and said we should frame this recipe on the kitchen wall so we don't lose it!! ^_^

I made this because I was looking for a pantry staples type of meal . It fit the bill perfectly . However , I did tweak it a little . I omitted the olives and bell pepper just because I didn’t have any . I added a fresh chopped jalapeño and used crushed tomatoes 28oz can in place of Rotel . I also added 2 extra cups of tomato juice for a thinner soup and a tap of salt and 2tsp of cayenne . Just cuz we like it spicy !
Very flavorful recipe! I substituted ground turkey for the beef and added 2 Tbs of Dutch cocoa powder to give a little richness to the end result.

Very good and quick recipe. I hadn't prepared it in the morning for my crockpot so just cooked in a pot on the stove until peppers were tender. It was still very quick. Although I love the taste of ranch seasoning, I never buy it in a store because it's loaded with msg. I found a recipe for a homemade mix that I keep on hand. For recipes that call for a packet, I use 1 tbsp of this mix. It's 1/2 c dry buttermilk, 1 tbsp dried parsley, 1 tsp dried dill weed, 1 tsp onion powder, 1 tsp dried onion flakes, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp black pepper. Blend in blender. Store in airtight container.

Excellent and easily adaptable to what you have on hand. I made only minor changes, but still followed the recipe. This came out the consistency of a chili, and no, I did not drain any of the cans. Everything in! I doubled the recipe, used a 28 ounce can of herb diced tomatoes, tomato passata and ground turkey. I finely chopped 1 hot fingerling pepper and this was the perfect kick for this huge amount. For garnish, I used shredded cheddar with habanero, chopped cilantro, sour cream and chipotle cheddar tortilla strips. Well worth making, and better the next day. Yum!!

We loved it and did not change anything! The original review was 2015. This is an update. This is 2025 and it is a staple at least once a month we have this. It is so delicious. I do add some chopped jalapeño peppers just enough to give it just a kiss of heat. As a reminder with extra cheese on top and a big dollop of sour cream. I could eat it for breakfast, lunch and dinner. And think about it is is so quick and so easy to make, and I throw it in a crockpot. So there’s no standing over the stove. Take about 3 to 4 hours on high for the vegetables to cook.

Made as written except I chose to sub jalapeno for the green bell because that just made sense to me. As written this is more of a chili than a soup so I'll just put that out there. Add some beef broth or water if you want a true soup consistency. The 15 ounce can of black olives must be a typo. They don't come in that size and that would be olive soup. I'm thinking that must be 1 5oz can. Overall a great soup. Simple and full of flavor. Fuss free as well. Keeper. Made as written and in chili form, this makes for a great topping for nachos. If making for a soup, add some liquid. That's my two cents.

Pretty good. Used red bell peppers for green, omitted the black olives for the audience, and added an 8oz can of tomato sauce (in addition to the recipe’s called for tomato juice). Result? Pretty tasty taco-like-chili. I did cook on low for closer to 8 hours and served with cheese, chips, green onions and sour cream. Fun, easy and glad we tried! Thanks MICHMEIG!
Used 1/2 jar of fire roasted red pepper instead of using 1 green pepper! I use this recipe a lot:)

Followed recipe except for the olives. It tasted good but I found the amount of spices in the recipe left it desiring more. I added more of the taco seasoning and more of the ranch seasoning, I also added another green chile. Add a dash of cayenne for my preference of heat. It is always a family favorite, not as heavy as chile.

This tasted like chili to me, but I love chili so I loved this too. I didn't have any green peppers from my garden so I left those out. I did add a little extra tomato juice to make it thinner, so maybe that is why I thought it tasted like chili. It was great though and my husband really liked it too. I made this a second time and it was spicy from the diced tomatoes with chilis.
